land.text: Cliopatria's Kidarite shape of 402 adds exactly the Xionite shape of 387-401

successors.note: Cliopatria's reading (ledger 401, confidence 1); the pages are silent on who held the land in 402.

land.text: Cliopatria's White Huns row begins in 410 with the same shape

successors.note: The same 488,436 km2 shape starts the White Huns row in 410: the white-huns dossier and this one should agree on a single heir.

capitals.name: Chach (Tashkent)
capitals.note: The page says only that 'Some Chionites are known to have ruled in Chach' from the mid-4th to the 6th century; it names no capital of the polity. A seat of some Chionites, not a documented capital.

correction.text: Transoxiana outside the Kidarite kingdom of 360-370: 'an ancient nomadic tribe of Transoxiana' (Grumbates page)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 353-386, no Cliopatria shape: the Chionites of Grumbates, 'an ancient nomadic tribe of Transoxiana', who 'between 353 AD and 358 CE ... attacked in the eastern frontiers' of the Sasanians, made peace in 358 and fought at Amida in 359. Extent is the page's word 'Transoxiana' less the Kidarite kingdom of 360-370; the page gives no boundary (about 0.25 M km2 on the gazetteer).

387-396, 488,436 km2 (62.3-78.4 E, 38.5-43.3 N: Transoxiana's north, the Syr Darya, Chach and Ferghana). The page places them in 'Transoxiana and Bactria', 'best documented in southern Central Asia from the late 4th century AD until the mid-5th century AD', with Chionites ruling at Chach; no area figure on the page, extent unverified. The shape takes in the Kidarite strip north of the Oxus (145 k km2) that the Kidarites left at the end of the 4th century.

397-401, same shape. The page's 'until the mid-5th century' runs 50 years past Cliopatria's 401; the Chionites are said to have ruled at Chach until the 6th century. Kept as drawn (ledger 401, confidence 1).

region.text: Transoxiana outside the Kidarite kingdom of 360-370: 'an ancient nomadic tribe of Transoxiana' (Grumbates page)

ledger.note: 353: the Chionites of Grumbates raid the Sasanian frontier. 'Between 353 AD and 358 CE, the Xionites under Grumbates attacked in the eastern frontiers of' Shapur II's empire; Grumbates is 'a king of the Chionitae', 'an ancient nomadic tribe of Transoxiana'. The Xionites page dates the first mention of the Chyon to 356 and the people's urheimat as 'uncertain'; the Hephthalites page has the Chionites 'arrived circa 350 CE'. Cliopatria's own row begins in 387.

region.text: the part of the 358 Kidarite shape inside the 387 Xionite shape: the north-of-the-Oxus strip

ledger.note: 387: the Xionites take the Oxus strip from the Kidarites. 'At the end of the 4th century AD, the Kidarites were pushed into Gandhara' (no year, no strip named); Cliopatria's Kidarite south shape and Xionite shape both begin in 387. Bridging judgment.

region.text: the Xionite shape of 387 east of Transoxiana proper: the Ferghana and Syr Darya side

ledger.note: 387: the Xionite shape reaches east to Ferghana and the Syr Darya. The page has Chionites at Chach and 'Transoxiana and Bactria' but no frontier; the eastern part of Cliopatria's 387 shape is bridged. Stateless land on these pages.

minus.text: Transoxiana outside the Kidarite kingdom of 360-370: 'an ancient nomadic tribe of Transoxiana' (Grumbates page)

region.text: the western part of Transoxiana outside the 387 shape

ledger.note: 387: the western and northern parts of Transoxiana (61.9-70.5 E, up to 45.9 N on the gazetteer) fall outside Cliopatria's 387 shape, which is narrower there than the keyframe 353-386. The pages are silent on why or who held it; bridging judgment.

401: Cliopatria's Xionite row ends. The page is silent on an end: it has the Xionites 'best documented ... until the mid-5th century AD' and Chionites ruling at Chach into the 6th, and scholars identifying Karmir Xyon with 'the Kidarites and/or Alchon'. The Kidarite shape of 402 and the White Huns shape of 410 both contain this land.

wars.name: Shapur II's war against the Chionites
wars.outcome: After a long struggle the war ended in 358 in a 'treaty alliance with the Chionites and the Gelani'; Grumbates then served Shapur II against Rome at the siege of Amida in 359, where his son was killed.
wars.note: The Xionites page says Shapur II 'waged war against the Xionites for ten years'; the Grumbates page gives 353-358 and the Amida siege of 359. Where the fighting lay is not named beyond 'the eastern frontiers' (Grumbates page); no zone is given.

certainty.note: Nomads of Transoxiana: no frontier is named on either page; the 358 treaty alliance with Shapur II fixed no line.

sources.title: Xionites
sources.note: Identity, the 356-358 contact, 'Transoxiana and Bactria', Chach, the Kidarites 'pushed into Gandhara' at the end of the 4th century; thin for 387-401 and without infobox (shared with the kidarites dossier).

sources.title: Grumbates
sources.note: 'Between 353 AD and 358 CE the Xionites under Grumbates attacked'; 'an ancient nomadic tribe of Transoxiana'; the siege of Amida in 359.

notes: Cliopatria: the row 387-401 is 488,436 km2 (62.3-78.4 E, 38.5-43.3 N) and ends in 401 although the page has Xionites documented to the mid-5th century and Chionites ruling at Chach into the 6th. The Kidarite shape of 402-442 is the Kidarite south shape plus this shape exactly (1,620 grid cells), and Cliopatria's White Huns row (410-450) is this shape again: two successors claim the land, so identity.successors lists both. Added: a keyframe 353-386 for the Chionites of the 350s (the page's 'Transoxiana' less the Kidarite kingdom of 360-370) because both pages date the Xionites well before 387; its extent is the researcher's reading of one word. Remove it if the reviewer prefers Cliopatria's 387 start. The three 387 events (two gains, one loss, all confidence 1) only account for the difference between that keyframe and the 387 shape. Page budget: two pages (Xionites, Grumbates). The Hephthalites and Kidarites pages opened for the kidarites dossier add: 'the Chionites (who arrived circa 350 CE)' and the Kidarites 'from around 380 CE' (Hephthalites page), against the Kidarites page's kingdom of 360-370. Not settled: the ten years of war (Xionites page) against five (353-358, Grumbates page); where Grumbates' people lived in 356-357 (the Xionites page has a fragment placing someone 'in Bactria during 356-357 AD'); the capital; what the Xionites became (Kidarites, White Huns or Alchon). No unknown gazetteer names. States needing dossiers: none new (Sasanian Empire, Kidarites and White Huns exist or are being written).
